newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican troop movements in Chiapas denounced.
newsitem.headline: Mexican troop movements in Chiapas denounced.
newsitem.dateline: SAN CRISTOBAL DE LAS CASAS, Mexico 1997-06-18

text.p: Church leaders in the troubled Mexican state of Chiapas said on Wednesday that army troop movements in the run-up to July 6 mid-term elections were undermining the chances of peace.

Catholic Bishop Samuel Ruiz told reporters "a widespread presence of troops" was causing concern among Indian communities in the Lacandon jungle, where guerrillas from the Zapatista National Liberation Army (EZLN) are concentrated.
Ruiz said he witnessed troop movements last week while he headed two widely attended religious pilgrimages in Indian villages in the southeastern Mexican state.
"The troops withdrew after I informed the commanding officer they were religious acts," Ruiz said.

Ruiz chairs the National Intermediation Commission (Conai) which mediates between the EZLN and the Mexican government. The EZLN launched an armed uprising against the government on Jan. 1, 1994, but the government called a ceasefire 10 days later.
Negotiations between the two sides have since taken place, although the EZLN withdrew from talks in September 1996 over differences concerning Indian rights.
Mexico will hold elections on July 6 to renew the entire lower chamber of Congress and one-fourth of the Senate.
Also on Wednesday, another bishop from San Cristobal denounced the expulsion of a Scottish priest as "arbitrary and absurd."
"This is another action within the framework of aggression by the government which the diocese and Catholic church have suffered for some time," Raul Vera told the local press.

Henry McCowling, parish priest at the Indian community of Huixtan, had his Mexican visa revoked after leaving the country on a return visit to Scotland, said Gonzalo Ituarte of the San Cristobal diocese.
Ituarte told Reuters Mexican immigration authorities had falesly accused McCowling of "undertaking religious acts without permission."
